transcript.text: Is it normal for my dishwasher to leave everything wet? Plastic tubs are soaking every time and there's drips on the glasses. It's a Bosch Serie 4.

Yes, it is normal for plastic tubs to remain wet; plastics do not retain heat well and often stay damp even when glassware is dry. However, glasses should generally be dry. The most common reason for wet glasses is low rinse aid or using a programme that skips the heated drying phase (like Eco). Please top up your rinse aid reservoir and try a standard cycle instead of an eco one. Have you topped up the rinse aid recently?
The rinse aid symbol is lit actually, so it's empty. I use all-in-one tablets though. I always run Eco 50, should I switch to something else?

Yes, you should switch to a standard cycle like 'Auto' or 'Normal'. The Eco 50 programme is designed to save energy by using lower temperatures and often skips the heated drying phase, which leaves water on surfaces. Plastic items will always stay damp because they don't hold heat, but glasses should be dry if the rinse aid is working correctly. Since your rinse aid symbol is lit, it is empty. All-in-one tablets contain a small amount of rinse aid, but it is rarely enough to prevent spotting and wetting on glassware. Please top up the rinse aid reservoir (usually located in the door) and run a standard cycle next time. This combination should resolve the dripping on your glasses.

candidates: Rinse aid level too low or programme choice not suited for drying (high)
